summary: Turned specs/database/postgres.sql into 13 forward-only numbered goose migrations under infra/migrations/ (v3.28.0, embedded, transactional, advisory-locked), preserving every table, column type, nullability, default, FK action, CHECK, UNIQUE and explicit index of the canonical schema. Stood up the pgx v5.11 + sqlc v1.31.1 data-access layer: 63 typed query methods generated from explicit SQL (internal/persistence/queries) and checked in (internal/persistence/sqlc) with a drift check that regenerates and diffs. Added panic-safe WithTx (rollback on error/panic, commit otherwise) and a task/run-scoped test database namespace (test_T0005_<run_id>, docs/66 §3, created and dropped per test). All required G1/G3 tests ran against REAL PostgreSQL (compose project posttask-t0005 on 127.0.0.1:15432): fresh-install catalog verified by querying pg_catalog against a 1:1 fixture of the canonical schema (37 tables + goose_db_version, 84 FKs, 16 uniques, all checks, 5 explicit indexes, vector+pgcrypto extensions), repeat migrate proven a byte-identical no-op, upgrade path (version 6 → head) proven indistinguishable from a fresh install, and 9 constraint violations rejected with exact SQLSTATEs (23503/23505/23514) including forbidden UPDATE and DELETE. Drift check exercised in BOTH modes: passing (clean) and failing (injected probe query detected with diff, tree restored). ops/doctor.sh still passes (exit 0). Docker stack torn down: no containers/volumes left behind for this project. L1 decision: pressly/goose as migration tool, recorded in infra/migrations/README.md.

tests.evidence: Container posttask-t0005-postgres-1 Healthy (pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg16 on 127.0.0.1:15432). All DB tests below ran against this real PostgreSQL.

ok github.com/lichman0405/post/tests/integration 1.882s — all 6 tests pass: TestFreshInstallCatalog (catalog fixture vs pg_catalog: 38 tables incl. goose_db_version, columns/types/nullability/defaults, PKs, 16 uniques, 84 FKs with exact RESTRICT/SET NULL actions, checks, 5 explicit GIN/btree indexes, extensions pgcrypto+plpgsql+vector), TestRepeatMigrateIsNoop (applied=0, version unchanged, catalog byte-identical), TestUpgradePath (MigrateTo(6) applies exactly 6; intermediate state has exactly the 00001-00006 tables and relation_versions_source_idx; Migrate to head applies 7; upgraded snapshot == fresh-install snapshot == canonical fixture), TestConstraintEnforcement, TestSQLCQueriesRoundTrip (typed query layer: user/org/project/branch/state/object/versions round-trip, append-only version log), TestWithTx, TestSQLCGenerationDrift.

9 real rejections with exact SQLSTATEs: DELETE FROM users referenced by projects.created_by → 23503 'update or delete on table "users" violates foreign key constraint "projects_created_by_fkey"'; DELETE FROM project_states referenced by scientific_object_versions.state_id → 23503 "scientific_object_versions_state_id_fkey"; UPDATE users SET handle (duplicate) → 23505 "users_handle_key"; UPDATE branches SET lifecycle_state='bogus' → 23514 "branches_lifecycle_state_check"; INSERT duplicate scientific_object_version version_no=1 → 23505 "scientific_object_versions_object_id_version_no_key"; INSERT version_no=0 → 23514 "scientific_object_versions_version_no_check"; INSERT organization_memberships role='admin' → 23514 "organization_memberships_role_check"; INSERT blobs size_bytes=-1 → 23514 "blobs_size_bytes_check"; INSERT policy_versions with both scopes → 23514 "policy_versions_check". Append-only flow itself still works (version 2 appends cleanly, 2 rows intact).
exit 0: 'DRIFT CHECK [verify]: clean — checked-in generated code matches generator output'. sqlc v1.31.1 regenerate + diff vs snapshot of checked-in internal/persistence/sqlc.

Both modes exercised as required. Failing mode: script injected '-- name: DriftProbeQuery :one / SELECT 42 AS answer;' into internal/persistence/queries/users.sql, regenerated, and the check FAILED with a real diff ('DRIFT CHECK [demo]: FAILED — regeneration differs from checked-in code': querier.go gained 'DriftProbeQuery(ctx context.Context) (int32, error)' and users.sql.go gained the generated method + query const). Tree then restored and regenerated by the EXIT trap; script exit 0 means detection demonstrably works. A drift check never observed failing is not evidence — this one was.

no findings, exit 0. (One style finding S1011 fixed during development; staticcheck also caught a structural flaw: tests/integration/catalog.go was a non-test file referencing declarations from _test.go files — renamed to catalog_test.go.)

acceptance.evidence: TestFreshInstallCatalog: empty namespaced database migrated to head (13/13 applied, goose version 13); the resulting catalog verified by querying pg_catalog/information_schema against a fixture derived 1:1 from specs/database/postgres.sql: 37 canonical tables + goose_db_version as the only extra, every column with exact type/nullability/default presence (incl. text[] udt '_text' and vector udt 'vector'), PKs, 16 unique constraints, 84 FKs with exact ON DELETE actions (83 RESTRICT, 1 SET NULL), all CHECK constraints, the 5 explicit indexes (gin payload, source/target btree, fts gin, structured gin) with correct definitions, and extensions pgcrypto+plpgsql+vector.

TestRepeatMigrateIsNoop: second Migrate applies 0 migrations, version stays 13, catalog snapshot byte-identical. TestUpgradePath: MigrateTo(6) applies exactly 6 and the intermediate state contains exactly the 00001-00006 tables; Migrate to head applies the remaining 7; the upgraded catalog is byte-identical to a fresh install AND matches the canonical fixture. Forward-only by design: no down migrations exist; infra/migrations/README.md documents the policy (numbered files immutable, changes = new higher number) and the upgrade path.

Passing mode: 'DRIFT CHECK [verify]: clean' (exit 0). Failing mode exercised and recorded: injected probe query → check FAILED with diff showing the new generated method in querier.go/users.sql.go → tree restored (exit 0). Same single implementation (tests/integration/check-sqlc-drift.sh) is wired into go test via TestSQLCGenerationDrift (skips only if the sqlc binary is absent, with the exact install command). sqlc v1.31.1 pinned in sqlc.yaml and README.

acceptance.evidence: TestConstraintEnforcement: 9 forbidden operations rejected with exact SQLSTATEs — FK RESTRICT blocks DELETE of referenced users (23503) and DELETE of project_states referenced by object versions (23503), UNIQUE blocks duplicate handle UPDATE (23505) and duplicate version INSERT (23505), CHECK blocks invalid lifecycle UPDATE (23514), version_no=0 (23514), role='admin' (23514), negative blob size (23514), and the policy_versions XOR (23514). Append-only append itself verified working (2 versions intact). TestWithTx additionally proves rollback-on-error, rollback-on-panic with panic re-raised, rollback under ctx cancellation, and commit on success.

risks: Canonical seed is not executable in file order: specs/database/postgres.sql creates project_states (which references branches(id) inline) before branches exists — PostgreSQL rejects that. The migration set creates branches first; no constraint was changed, only statement order, and branches_base_state_fk is still added via the canonical ALTER TABLE. Documented in infra/migrations/README.md §Deviations; flagged for Supervisor confirmation.

go.mod and go.sum were modified (pgx v5.11.0, goose v3.28.0 + indirects). Per the worker environment contract these are assigned to T0005; the other in-flight worker was told not to touch them. sqlc itself is a dev-time tool (go install github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc/cmd/sqlc@v1.31.1), not a module dependency, so it does not appear in go.mod.

goose's bookkeeping table goose_db_version (id, version_id, is_applied, tstamp) is the only non-canonical table in the public schema and is asserted as such in the test fixture. If a future task wants a different table name, use goose.WithStore.
Migration tool choice is an L1 decision: pressly/goose v3.28.0 as a library (golang-migrate and a hand-rolled runner were considered and rejected; rationale in infra/migrations/README.md).

The drift Go test (TestSQLCGenerationDrift) skips when the sqlc binary is unavailable, with an explicit skip reason and install command. CI wiring (.github/workflows, Makefile) is outside T0005's allowed_scope; the Supervisor should ensure CI installs sqlc v1.31.1 and runs the integration tests with a PostgreSQL service, otherwise the drift check will skip there.

Add pgvector/embedding queries to internal/persistence/queries/search.sql when the V1 search work (docs/14) needs vector similarity; currently only FTS is exposed, which is all V1 requires.

notes_for_supervisor: Docker grant used as instructed: compose project posttask-t0005, postgres on 127.0.0.1:15432 (POSTGRES_PORT=15432), down -v afterwards — nothing left behind, the T0003 stack on 5432 untouched. Two implementation gotchas worth knowing: (1) pgx's ConnConfig.ConnString() returns the ORIGINAL parsed string, so rewriting cfg.ConnConfig.Database is a silent no-op — internal/persistence/testdb.WithDatabase rewrites the URL with net/url instead (this bug initially made all tests share the admin database; caught by the tests themselves and fixed). (2) staticcheck compiles non-test files without _test.go files, so test machinery must live in _test.go files — tests/integration/catalog_test.go. sqlc config uses the migration files themselves as its schema input, so generated code always matches what migrations ship — no shadow schema copy. All test evidence commands are in the tests[] array with real observed output; nothing was skipped except the two doctor checks that are opt-in by design.
